alex.support: FYI customer reports private endpoint stopped accepting mTLS after scheduled cert swap this morning. Clients see 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. They claim no config changes on their side. acme-sre: Confirmed, started failing around 08:12 UTC, we see client TLS handshakes aborting with alert unknown_ca. alex.support: Can you paste the client error and the vip SNI? acme-sre: SNI is api-acme.internal.redwood.net, client error attached: `tls: handshake failure: tls: certificate signed by unknown authority` tim.oncall: Quick triage — sounds like server still presenting old cert or missing intermediate. Can you run an openssl s_client against the VIP from within their VPC? Command: ```openssl s_client -connect api-acme.internal.redwood.net:443 -servername api-acme.internal.redwood.net -showcerts``` acme-sre: Ran it, here's the cert chain snippet we got: ```Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=old-service.acme
   i:/CN=acme-rotator-temp
 1 s:/CN=acme-rotator-temp
   i:/CN=acme-root
``` acme-sre: The leaf is the old-service cert (expires soon) not the new one we'd expected. rotator-bot: rotation-job 2026-03-17T07:58:03Z for tenant acme completed successfully, uploaded files to /var/lib/rotator/acme/20260317-0758 and signalled reload via systemctl reload haproxy.service rotator-bot: rotator logs show exit code 0 for upload + reload call. ingrid.platform: Interesting — upload + systemctl reload might not cause HAProxy to re-open cert fds depending on our packaging. If HAProxy was started with --disable-systemd-cgroup or the package's reload doesn't do a full re-exec, it can keep old file descriptors. tim.oncall: Can ops check what cert file HAProxy process actually has open? On the host run: `lsof -p $(pgrep haproxy) | grep -E "\.pem|\.crt"` acme-sre: Ran lsof, output: ```haproxy  23045 haproxy  3r  REG  253,1 2048  /etc/haproxy/certs/acme.pem``` acme-sre: But the timestamp on /etc/haproxy/certs/acme.pem is updated. tim.oncall: Do a `ss -xp | grep haproxy` and also `cat /proc/23045/fdinfo/3` to confirm fd points to deleted vs current inode. acme-sre: `readlink /proc/23045/fd/3` -> `/etc/haproxy/certs/acme.pem` `stat /etc/haproxy/certs/acme.pem` shows inode 131072, but `ls -l /proc/23045/fd/3` points to inode 130400. Looks like HAProxy still has the old inode open. alex.support: So rotator replaced the file (new inode) but HAProxy kept old fd. That matches a reload command that didn't cause a full re-exec or reopen(2) on cert file. tim.oncall: Short fix: restart haproxy process (systemctl restart haproxy) or trigger a full re-exec so it reopens fds. acme-sre: We restarted haproxy and client TLS errors cleared immediately. acme-sre: :thumbsup: thanks. ingrid.platform: Next steps: we'll update rotator to signal haproxy with a full reopen path. Two options: 1) call `haproxy -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg -p /run/haproxy.pid -sf $(cat /run/haproxy.pid)` for seamless binary re-exec, or 2) ensure the systemd unit's Reload= triggers ExecReload that does an actual reopen. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to change the rotator reload hook to use the re-exec pattern. rotator-bot: created issue RNW-INF-4832 (rotator: ensure services get full re-exec/reopen on cert update) alex.support: Also adding a KB for support steps: how to verify fd inode mismatch and safe restart. acme-sre: Appreciate the quick turnaround. tim.oncall: Filing follow-up to look for other tenants that had reload-only rotate events in last 24h, to proactively restart or nudge. alex.support: closing thread once eng-runtime confirms PR.
